algorithm.Title: Hearing Loss or Change - Female (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Female
Definition: Hearing loss/change assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published when-to-get-help guidance.

KeyPoints: Hearing loss may be gradual or sudden, temporary or permanent, and can have treatable causes such as infection or earwax.
Sudden hearing loss or deterioration over days or weeks requires urgent assessment.
In children, hearing loss can affect speech development and school progress; caregiver observations are clinically important.
Background.ExpertReviewer: PENDING: Qatar adult, pediatric, obstetric, emergency, ENT, safeguarding, and nursing governance review

FirstAid: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive when hearing change follows major head trauma or accompanies stroke signs, severe vertigo with inability to stand, seizure, reduced consciousness, severe headache/neck stiffness, or fluid/blood from the ear after injury. Keep the person still; do not insert drops, tools, or packing into the ear and do not remove an embedded object. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is ear pain the main concern without new hearing loss or hearing change?
questions.Information: Primary ear pain without hearing change belongs in the earache pathway.

questions.Question: Does this sound like a life-threatening emergency to the triager (e.g. associated with a head injury or stroke symptoms)?
questions.Information: Universal emergency rule-out added ahead of the hearing loss guidance itself - hearing loss is rarely an emergency on its own, but must not mask trauma or a neurological event.

questions.Question: Did the hearing loss come on suddenly in one or both ears, has it worsened over just the last few days or weeks, or does it come with earache or discharge?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends an urgent clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) or the Qatar clinical-review pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) call for sudden hearing loss or hearing loss with other symptoms - it may need to be treated quickly.

questions.Question: Has the hearing been getting gradually worse over time, or did it not improve after treatment for an ear infection or earwax?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends a routine clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) for gradual hearing changes or hearing that hasn't improved after prior treatment.

advice.Title: Qatar emergency hearing-loss response
Content: Call Qatar emergency services on 999 and do not drive when hearing change follows major head trauma or accompanies stroke signs, severe vertigo with inability to stand, seizure, reduced consciousness, severe headache/neck stiffness, or fluid/blood from the ear after injury. Keep the person still; do not insert drops, tools, or packing into the ear and do not remove an embedded object. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: neurological change or reduced consciousness; severe vertigo or inability to stand; blood or clear fluid after head injury.

advice.Title: Urgent hearing review
Content: Arrange an urgent clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) or the Qatar clinical-review pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) assessment - sudden hearing changes may need quick treatment.
Call Back If: hearing worsens further; dizziness develops.

advice.Title: Routine hearing follow-up
Content: Book a routine clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED); a free hearing test may also be available at some pharmacies and opticians.
Call Back If: sudden worsening; new ear pain or discharge.
